title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 19, 2026: KOSPI Rebounds 1.76%, ESS Battery Stocks and KBI Dongyang Rise
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,768.01, up 1.76%, and KOSDAQ closed at 808.89, up 1.78%, as dip buying lifted both indexes after last week's sharp selloff. Individual themes moved on their own news: energy storage (ESS) orders ahead of battery makers' third-quarter results, a China licensing evaluation deal for G2GBIO, and KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe's supply to SpaceX launch facilities.

1. Dip buying after the plunge — KOSPI and KOSDAQ rebound together

Korean markets, which sold off sharply last week on U.S. inflation and interest rate pressure and worries about the profitability of AI infrastructure investment, rebounded as investors bought on the view that the drop had been overdone. KOSPI closed at 5,768.01 (+1.76%) and KOSDAQ at 808.89 (+1.78%). Both indexes hit their lows early in the session and then widened their gains, recovering part of the shock from last week.

2. ESS orders and third-quarter earnings hopes — battery stocks rise

Ahead of the third-quarter results of Korea's three battery makers, expanding North American ESS orders and rising power demand from AI data centers pushed battery stocks higher. With electric vehicle growth slowing, expectations are growing that ESS could become a new growth driver for Korean battery makers. In the U.S., investment in AI data centers and the power grid is expanding, and demand for local supply chains to replace Chinese batteries is also rising, lifting hopes for orders and profitability. Large battery names such as Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution and SK Innovation rose, and buying spread to materials, parts and equipment stocks.

As ESS installations expand to keep AI data centers powered reliably, benefits can spread beyond cells to thermal management, safety parts and cases. Actual ESS revenue share and benefit differ by company. Today's key driver was ESS growth hopes across the battery sector rather than solid-state materials specifically, even though solid-state batteries, which replace the liquid electrolyte with a solid one to improve safety and energy density, drew some attention.

3. G2GBIO signs a China UBT evaluation deal — long-acting injectable platform hopes

Bio platform stocks drew attention after G2GBIO said it signed an evaluation agreement with China's UBT for its long-acting injectable platform. G2GBIO owns a long-acting drug delivery platform (InnoLAMP) that packs a drug into tiny particles designed to release it slowly in the body, which can extend how long a drug works or reduce dosing frequency, and its potential for technology cooperation and commercialization with global drugmakers is in focus. Buying spread to bio platform and technology names including Rznomics, D&D Pharmatech and Curiox Biosystems. This is an evaluation-stage contract, which should be distinguished from a large technology transfer or confirmed commercialization, and the other companies do not all have direct contracts with G2GBIO, so their business links should be checked separately.

4. KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe supplies steel pipe to SpaceX — space and steel pipe stocks rise

KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe hit its daily upper limit on news that it is supplying about 950 tons of high-strength steel pipe to U.S. space company SpaceX's rocket launch facilities. The pipe is not part of the rocket itself but material for the launch pad's water deluge system, which sprays large amounts of water to reduce the heat and shock of launch. The company said it shipped 640 tons in April and is supplying an additional 205 tons and 105 tons in October. Buying spread to steel pipe and valve names such as Dongil Steellux and Hwaseong Valve and to space-themed stocks such as HVM and Sphere. KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe has an actual supply record, while the other stocks moved largely because they are in related industries, so direct supply to SpaceX should be distinguished.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI and KOSDAQ rise on Oct 19?
Dip buying came in after last week's sharp selloff on U.S. inflation and rate pressure and AI investment profitability worries. KOSPI closed at 5,768.01 (+1.76%) and KOSDAQ at 808.89 (+1.78%).

Why were battery stocks strong?
Ahead of the battery makers' third-quarter results, expanding North American ESS orders and rising AI data center power demand stood out. ESS revenue share differs by company.

Does KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe make SpaceX rocket parts?
No. The company says it supplies pipe for the launch pad's water deluge system, not the rocket. Other steel pipe, valve and space stocks rose mainly as related industries, not because of direct supply.
